rationale: Keep Durham Region Courthouse as a standalone operational infrastructure asset and reject the earlier conceptual-portfolio merge. INPP's and Amber's current official case studies each report 100% equity ownership, operational status, a March 2007 financial close and a 30-year term from construction completion. Infrastructure Ontario identifies Access Justice Durham as the DBFM consortium and confirms completion in 2009. Add the legal project-company alias, normalize the manager name, record the officially disclosed 100% stake, improve the location and description, refresh milestone evidence, and make INPP's current project page the primary citation.

beforeImage.name: Durham Region Courthouse
beforeImage.description: Durham Region Courthouse is a judicial public-private partnership in Ontario. The project serves the provincial court system and related users through a long-term availability-based concession covering facility delivery and lifecycle responsibilities. Public materials identify the asset within Amber-managed judicial infrastructure portfolios rather than as a demand-exposed commercial property. The courthouse reached financial close in 2007 and has been held through infrastructure investment vehicles associated with Amber and International Public Partnerships. Reviewed public sources do not disclose the current project-level ownership split.

milestones.event: The project received an Award of Merit for project financing from the Canadian Council for Public-Private Partnerships.
BBPP / INPP, now advised by Amber Infrastructure, acquired the Durham Region Courthouse project company at financial close.

afterImage.name: Durham Region Courthouse
afterImage.description: Durham Region Courthouse is an operational judicial public-private partnership in Oshawa, Ontario. Access Justice Durham Limited is responsible for the financing, maintenance and lifecycle renewal of the approximately 440,000-square-foot courthouse, which consolidates Superior Court and Ontario Court of Justice services in 33 courtrooms. Babcock & Brown Public Partnerships, INPP's predecessor, acquired 100% of the project-company equity at financial close in March 2007. INPP and Amber currently report 100% equity ownership and a 30-year term from construction completion; Infrastructure Ontario records construction completion in November 2009.
